prose: A field guide to building an AI-native software factory, mixing quotes and hard numbers. On economics: if LLMs add $1,000/month per engineer for 10% more productivity, that's too cheap - spend more. On review queues: PostHog merges ~200 PRs a day, and an analysis of one day's merges found the median wait for a first human review is 6.1 hours with a 90th percentile of 160.8 hours - and 40% of PRs merged with no human review at all (bot reviewers like CodeRabbit see nearly every PR within 4 minutes).

Practical advice threads through: use 'claude -p' in CI to triage failed builds, summarize flaky tests and draft changelogs; don't try to recreate Copilot, Cursor or Replit in-house; expect failed first attempts, like one company's unsuccessful multi-file test migration. The emotional undercurrent is captured in one engineer's line: after 25 years of programming, feeling competent in that skill set is ending.
highlights: PostHog data: median first human PR review takes 6.1 hours; p90 is 160.8 hours.
40% of PRs merged with no human review; bots review most PRs within ~4 minutes.
Advice: LLM spend that buys 10% productivity for $1,000/month is too cheap.
Use 'claude -p' in pipelines for build triage, flaky-test summaries and changelogs.
One engineer's epitaph: 25 years of programming competence reaching the end of an era.
